title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
prompt:
Build a class that answers "what is the total of nums[from..to]?" (both ends included) for an array that never changes. There may be up to 10^5 queries, so each query must be O(1): do the work once in the constructor.

  • new RangeSum(nums): precompute whatever you need.
  • sum(from, to): returns nums[from] + ... + nums[to]. You can assume 0 <= from <= to < nums.length.

Example: const r = new RangeSum([20, 35, 0, 15, 40, 25, 30]);

  • r.sum(2, 5) → 80 (0 + 15 + 40 + 25)
  • r.sum(0, 0) → 20
  • r.sum(0, 6) → 165

Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5, values may be negative.

tests.name: single-element ranges (catches off-by-one)
negative numbers
many queries agree with a brute-force loop

hints: Trigger: many range-sum queries on an array that never changes. That's prefix sums: pay O(n) once, then O(1) per query.
Idea: store prefix[i] = the total of the first i numbers, with prefix[0] = 0. The sum from from to to is "everything through to" minus "everything before from".
Code shape: in the constructor, this.prefix = [0]; for (const x of nums) this.prefix.push(this.prefix[this.prefix.length - 1] + x);. In sum: return this.prefix[to + 1] - this.prefix[from];
explain:
Constructor O(n) time and O(n) space; each sum O(1). For q queries that's O(n + q) instead of O(n · q). The leading 0 in the prefix array is what makes ranges starting at index 0 work without a special case.

In real systems this is the same idea as storing a running balance in a ledger, or pre-aggregated daily totals in an analytics table so a dashboard can sum any date range from a few rows.

How to say it: "The array is static and there are many queries, so I'll precompute prefix sums in O(n). Any range sum is then prefix[to + 1] minus prefix[from], O(1). If the array were updated between queries, I'd reach for a Fenwick tree instead."
